summary.headline: Ahead of target on orders and revenue, and the quarter is running ahead; but the year sits barely above target and needs a faster pace than recent weeks.

points.what: Orders came in at 1,157, or 117.8% of the weekly target, and up 106.2% on last year.
points.so_what: The week cleared its volume target, with growth running faster than the targets assume.

points.what: Revenue was $86,556, or 108.4% of the weekly target, but down 2.6% week on week, which is rated bad.
points.so_what: The week beat its revenue target even though revenue moved down against the prior week.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is 100.3% of the target to date.
points.so_what: The year's margin above target is thin, so a run of weaker weeks would tip the year behind.

points.what: Orders are flagged as notable because the week's count sits outside the 8-week range, against an 8-week average of 1,054.
points.so_what: This week's volume should be treated as unusual rather than as the new weekly level.

points.what: Hitting the full-year target requires $85,110 of revenue a week for the remaining 22 weeks, against a current 8-week run-rate of $77,852.
points.so_what: The rest of the year demands more per week than recent weeks have delivered, putting the full-year target at risk.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose 0.5 pp to 15.3%, rated bad, and each percentage point is worth $1,022 of revenue.
points.so_what: The increase worked against revenue in a week when revenue already fell versus the prior week.

points.what: New signups of 254 were down 4.9% on last year, rated bad, while orders were up 106.2% on last year.
points.so_what: The two year-on-year growth measures point in opposite directions, so order growth is not matched on the signup side.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue of $403,276 is 114.7% of the target to date, five weeks into the quarter.
points.so_what: The quarter has built a cushion against target, but it is only settled once the remaining weeks are in.

points.what: $584,720 of the $987,996 full-quarter target is still outstanding with 8 weeks left.
points.so_what: Most of the quarter's target is still ahead, so the current cushion is not decisive for the quarter.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is 100.3% of target, with January to April behind target and May to July ahead.
points.so_what: The year is only marginally ahead, and that position rests entirely on the recent run of months.

points.what: EMEA orders rose 26.1% to 251 and contributed 52 of the week's order increase, or 208% of the change.
points.so_what: EMEA accounts for more than the entire weekly gain, so the total increase depends on one region.

points.what: North America orders fell 13.2% to 224, a contribution of -34 orders.
points.so_what: North America pulled against the weekly increase, and it is the only region growing more slowly year on year than the targets assume.

points.what: Search, the largest source at 69.1% of orders, contributed 15 orders, or 60% of the week's change.
points.so_what: The weekly order gain rests on the largest source rather than on a shift between sources.

points.what: AOV was $88.32, down 4.1% week on week, which is rated bad, though up 2.7% on last year.
points.so_what: Read with the higher order count, the week's revenue decline sits with lower value per order rather than volume.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 13 July was 10.0%, down 0.5 pp on the week before and 1.7 pp on last year, both rated good.
points.so_what: Returns are the one order-quality measure moving in the right direction, offsetting part of the AOV and cancellation movement.

points.what: New signups were 254, up 9.5% week on week, which is rated good, against order growth of 2.2%.
points.so_what: Week on week, signup growth ran ahead of order growth, the reverse of the year-on-year comparison.

checks.name: 14-Day Return Rate names its mature week
anomaly flag acknowledged in the summary
sentences at most 30 words and 4 numbers
each slot only covers its allowed KPIs
